blocks.text: Startup ordering covers only `docker compose up` on one host; databases restart, IPs change and orchestrators don't order startup, so the app must tolerate temporarily unavailable dependencies.
Startup: bounded wait, then fail loudly

blocks.code:
@retry(stop=stop_after_delay(60), wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=0.5, max=5),
       retry=retry_if_exception_type(OperationalError), reraise=True)
async def wait_for_db(engine):
    async with engine.connect() as c:
        await c.execute(text("SELECT 1"))

blocks.text: Bounded matters: an infinite wait hides a wrong hostname; after the deadline, exit 1 and let the restart policy retry.

items: `pool_pre_ping=True`: dead pooled connections are replaced after a DB restart.
`pool_recycle`: cap connection age behind proxies and load balancers.
Retry idempotent calls (searches, embeddings) with backoff and jitter; make writes idempotent (upsert by chunk ID) before retrying them.
Timeouts everywhere; a missing timeout turns an outage into hung workers.

blocks.text: Q: "Why isn't condition: service_healthy enough?" A: "It only orders the initial compose up. Runtime restarts, failovers and Kubernetes aren't covered. The app needs bounded startup retries, pre-ping pools, timeouts and retries on idempotent calls."
